decision: Does TensorLBM acquire TCLB's model-dir-as-build-and-CI-unit property — (a) model units discovered by enumeration, (b) build targets and CI matrix generated from those directories, (c) each unit carrying its own analytic reference and tolerance, (d) adding a model touching only its own directory — with the property measured at the owner 15% criterion?

alternatives.A1_status_quo: monolithic CI job + hand-written matrices (current ci.yml / validation-matrix slot list); no per-model build unit
alternatives.A2_central_registry: one central registry file (models.py dict) that maps names to kernels; units not self-describing; adding a model edits 2+ files
alternatives.A3_dir_as_unit: TCLB practice: directory = unit; manifest per directory; enumeration discovery (git ls-files + find union); generated Makefile targets and generated CI matrix (fromJSON); per-unit case + tolerance in the manifest

hypothesis: H1: A3 reproduces TCLB's organisational invariants with (i) 0% of units missing from the CI matrix, (ii) 0 hand-written unit names in the CI configuration, (iii) 0 files outside a new unit's directory needing edits, (iv) every unit passing its own <15% analytic check. H0 (falsifier): any of (i)-(iv) violated.

metrics.C1_ci_uncovered_frac: fraction of discovered model units absent from the CI matrix
metrics.C1b_hand_written_names: count of unit names literally present in the CI workflow file
metrics.C2_add_model_outside_edits: files outside the new unit directory that must change for discovery+build+matrix
metrics.C3_isolation_ratio: modules imported by one unit's build / modules shipped by the library
metrics.C4_verified_frac: fraction of units built and verified against an analytic reference below 15%
metrics.C4b_unit_kpi: each unit's declared KPI: Poiseuille profile sup-norm error vs analytic parabola; Taylor-Green decay-rate error vs 2*nu*k^2

unit_of_analysis: one model unit directory; aggregate metrics are fractions/counts over the discovered set

baseline_control.baseline: the TCLB checkout at /tmp/TCLB measured at run time (61 model dirs, 16 on the GH CPU matrix, 1 model-local check.py)
baseline_control.control: the same TensorLBM units run twice (deterministic build probe checksum equality) and the same KPI computed for two lattices / two case types

predeclared_thresholds.interpretation: every got-column value must satisfy its own bound; the TCLB (ref) value is reported alongside but judged separately, because TCLB drifts from its own generation rule
predeclared_thresholds.no_post_hoc_relaxation: a failing unit is reported failed and its threshold is not changed after seeing results

stopping_rule: each physics case runs the fixed step count declared in its model.toml; sensitivity sweeps use fixed ladders (ny 16/32/64, steps 500/1500/3000, tau 0.6/0.8/1.2, n 16/32/64) fixed before the run
confounders: TCLB cannot be compiled/run here (gcc/OpenCL/R toolchain absent), so the comparison is on organisational invariants extracted from its source, not on its runtime numbers
TensorLBM units are Python, so 'build' is an import closure + probe rather than a compiled binary; the isolation metric is therefore a proxy, reported as an absolute bound (C3)
CI matrix coverage of TCLB is measured from its GitHub workflow, which may lag its model.R enumeration by design (models built only locally)
repetition_rationale: deterministic solvers: repetition is replaced by (a) two lattices D2Q9/D3Q19, (b) two case families (forced channel, decaying vortex), (c) repeated build probe for determinism, (d) three sensitivity ladders
analysis: aggregate = the comparison rows written to artifacts/xval_m17991/xval.json; outliers = none expected (deterministic); the decision is A3 adopted iff all got-column rows pass
